nodes.title: MEA-CartPole: ready for the first live culture
nodes.notes: Each item is a chunk of the system to get working, or a decision the leads need to make. Open a chunk to see what it needs, the known bugs found in the code, and which files to start from. Work toward the milestones in order: rig works, then the full loop on saline, then the first culture.

nodes.title: 1B. Functional mapping and stimulus calibration
Adopt the adapted UCSC mapping method as standard?
nodes.notes: Syrine's proposal: one unit per electrode, baseline-corrected C1 (C1 minus chance), one-sided test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q = 0.05, windows 10 and 18 ms starting after the blind period, burst trials excluded (median + 3 MAD), map twice before training and once after. Already written as v2_ours_adapted.py. Also decide: does mapping fit on the same day as training (two maps of about 40 min plus a 2.5 h session)?
options: Adopt, but map once before training to save time
Skip mapping for the first cultures

nodes.title: Encoding scheme for the first cultures
nodes.notes: Current Baseline code encodes only which side the pole leans (sign of angle) and ignores angular velocity. v2 proposes: angle picks 1 of 6 input electrodes (bins 0-2, 2-6, 6-12 degrees per side), angular velocity sets a 10-40 Hz pulse rate, as a continuous train. nodes.title: 2B. Sensory stimulation
Which code path runs the loop?
nodes.notes: Both candidates are Python via pythonnet. The docs and CLAUDE.md call Baseline-Protocol/Hardware the active path, but all of Ryan's Oct 24 branches fix Hardware-Pythonnet-Path, and no branch fixes Baseline-Protocol. The C# files (Program.cs, MCS_interface.cs, Stimulator) are not in this repo; they live in the older Wetware and kaiorta-hash repos. Pick one path, archive the other, and only move to C# if measured pythonnet latency misses the budget.
options: C# loop, only if pythonnet misses the latency budget

nodes.title: Stimulation mode and pulse shape: voltage or current, which polarity?
nodes.notes: Baseline code: voltage mode, anodic-first, 75 mV x 200 us. Saline kit: cathodic-first, supports current mode (Abbas notes cathodic-first as agreed). Encoding v2: voltage, positive-first (Wagenaar 2004). In those papers polarity follows mode, so the real choice is voltage vs current. Use one mode for mapping, encoding and feedback.

options: Measure both on saline, then pick by artifact size and blind window

nodes.title: Feedback design: which paradigm, success bar and timing?
nodes.notes: Competing proposals: (a) v2 DishBrain-style structured vs unstructured, bar = rank against the last 20 episodes; (b) Saachi: no stimulation while the pole is up, 5-pulse 100 Hz burst on failure; (c) Saachi: Robbins adaptive training pairs. Also decide the success bar (rank vs last 20, or 85th percentile of baseline) and when structured feedback fires (milestone while the pole is up, or end of episode). Each extra arm needs 8+ more cultures.

nodes.spec: culture is the unit, 8+ per arm

nodes.title: Analysis plan, written before training data exists
nodes.notes: Agreed: the culture is the sample, 8+ per arm. Proposed: primary metric is mean log episode length in the final third vs chance (about 22 steps) and vs the dish's own baseline; secondary is final third minus first third; bootstrap CIs and permutation tests; homeostasis tracked as whole-dish rate per minute. Reference levels from offline_checks.py: stuck 9.4, chance 22.7, reflex 29.5 to 42.7 steps.
